section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes the findings of a single study conducted on 309 Portuguese women. The study aimed to test a model exploring the effects of social safeness, self-reassurance, and body-image appreciation on eating psychopathology symptoms. Key findings indicate that social safeness is linked to self-reassurance and a positive body relationship, with self-reassurance mediating the association between social safeness and body appreciation. The section also addresses limitations, including the cross-sectional design, reliance on self-report measures, and the exclusively female Portuguese sample, suggesting directions for future research.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes a single study conducted on 309 Portuguese women, which aimed to test a model exploring the effects of social safeness, self-reassurance, and body appreciation on eating psychopathology symptoms. The study found that social safeness is linked to self-reassurance and positive body image, with self-reassurance mediating the association between social safeness and body appreciation. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, exclusive use of self-report measures, and a female-only sample, suggesting future research should replicate hypotheses in different samples, including males and clinical populations.
